problem_motivation.content: The role of chemical short-range ordering (SRO) on dislocation mobilities in RHEAs needs investigation despite their known energetic driving force.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: However, they can also display a significant energetic driving force for chemical short-range ordering (SRO).

problem_motivation.content: There is a lack of detailed investigations regarding the effects of short-range order (SRO) on larger-scale defect properties, specifically dislocation mobility, in bcc RHEAs.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: To our knowledge, to date, there are no detailed investigations of the effects of SRO on larger-scale defect properties, especially dislocation mobility, for bcc RHEAs.

prior_approach.content: Citation of previous ML potentials and MTP framework in Nb–Ta–Mo–W systems.
prior_approach.evidence_span: We employ the general framework of machine-learning (ML)-based approaches, which have emerged recently as a systematic framework to develop potentials with accuracies near that of the underlying DFT calculations for elemental and multicomponent systems [24] , [44] – [46] .

prior_approach.content: Previous studies utilized a more generalized ordering parameter developed by Ceguerra for characterizing ordering.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Instead of the more generalized ordering parameter developed by Ceguerra [64]

prior_limitation.content: Despite theoretical and computational work on RHEAs, studies on their unique deformation behavior remain limited compared to pure bcc metals.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: However, compared to pure bcc metals, there are still limited studies on the unique deformation behavior of bcc RHEAs.

prior_limitation.content: Previous spectral neighbor analysis potential (SNAP) showed higher force errors compared to the current MTP implementation.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: While the mean absolute errors (MAEs) of energies of 4.6 and 4.3 meV atom −1 for respective training and test data are similar to those reported for previously developed potentials [24] , the MAEs of forces were decreased by half using the present implementation of MTP, compared to the previous spectral neighbor analysis potential (SNAP) [24] .

prior_limitation.content: The classical Fisher model predicts athermal SRO strengthening, which contradicts the observed temperature dependence.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: However, in this model the strengthening effect of SRO is athermal and should also be observed at higher temperatures, contrary to what is observed in the current simulation data.

rejected_alternative.content: The authors explicitly chose not to use Ceguerra's generalized ordering parameter, opting for the simpler pairwise multicomponent SRO parameter instead.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: Instead of the more generalized ordering parameter developed by Ceguerra [64] , we adopted a simpler pairwise multicomponent SRO parameter, specifically the Warren Cowley order parameter [65]

causal_claim.content: The presence of SRO enhances the mobility of edge dislocations.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The mobility of edge dislocations is found to be enhanced by the presence of SRO

causal_claim.content: The presence of SRO reduces the rate of double-kink nucleation in screw dislocation motion.
causal_claim.evidence_span: whereas the rate of double-kink nucleation in the motion of screw dislocations is reduced

causal_claim.content: The influence of SRO on dislocation mechanisms is attenuated as temperature increases.
causal_claim.evidence_span: although this influence of SRO appears to be attenuated at increasing temperature

causal_claim.content: The observed cross-slip locking mechanism provides extra strengthening to the RHEA system.
causal_claim.evidence_span: which provides for extra strengthening for refractory high-entropy alloy system

causal_claim.content: Increasing temperature reduces the critical stress required for screw dislocation glide.
causal_claim.evidence_span: As the temperature increases, the critical stress to initiate screw dislocation glide is progressively reduced.

hypothesis_statement.content: Hypothesis that SRO reduces solute drag, thereby enhancing edge dislocation mobility.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: One reasonable hypothesis is that the existence of SRO can also influence the solute interactions and, as such, lower the solute drag effect to enhance the mobility of the edge dislocation.

evidence_result.content: Screw dislocation velocity is significantly reduced due to cross-slip locking events.
evidence_result.evidence_span: the circles show anomalous points yielding a significantly lower average velocity, associated with the formation of cross-slip locking.

evidence_result.content: Screw dislocation glide velocity decreases with stress in RSS samples, showing kink-pair nucleation behavior.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Figure 3c shows the displacement vs. time results for a screw dislocation in the simulation with 1.4 GPa shear stress in the RSS sample, where it can be seen that the dislocation moves initially at a constant velocity via the kink-pair nucleation and migration mechanism

evidence_result.content: Edge dislocation velocity is highest when SRO is preserved in neighboring planes, decreasing as these layers are randomized.
evidence_result.evidence_span: It is observed that the dislocation velocity is highest in the sample with the highest degree of SRO, i.e., only order on the slip plane has been destroyed. With more layers of atoms around the slip plane being randomized, the RSS region becomes thicker and the average dislocation velocity keeps decreasing.

constraint.content: The simulation setup imposes a specific limit on the shear stress ramping rate to minimize stress wave effects.
constraint.evidence_span: the applied shear stress was gradually ramped [71] from zero at a rate of 20 MPa per 1.5 ps

contradiction.content: Observation of edge dislocation glide at low stress with SRO contradicts the established theory that SRO requires extra energy to break up.
contradiction.evidence_span: This is in contradiction with previous understanding [48] that the onset of dislocation glide necessitates the break-up of local order on the slip plane, which requires extra energy and stress.
